mstts:express-as.prosody: Living With Open Hearts. In the years after losing their daughter, the couple found a way to honor her memory—by keeping their hearts open. They traveled back to Haiti again and again, supporting the orphanage and staying close to the children who reminded them so much of the girl they’d loved and lost. They shared their story, not for sympathy, but to spark compassion and understanding in others. Most people? Well, most of us are a little afraid to open ourselves up to love. There’s that fear of loss, or maybe just the risk of being let down. But here’s what the couple realized: the only way to really live is to embrace vulnerability—to care deeply, even when you don’t know how things will turn out. Love doesn’t protect us from pain. Instead, it’s a promise. It’s a choice to show up, to be present, and to keep loving, no matter what happens. Of course, there were moments of doubt. Times when grief felt so heavy, it almost shut them off from the world. But every time, they’d remember the girl’s courage—the way she’d faced each new day with hope, even when the odds were stacked against her. That memory gave them strength. They chose, again and again, to keep their hearts open, to keep loving, and to believe that joy was still possible. Their journey wasn’t easy. And that pain of loss? It never really went away. But something beautiful happened—they found purpose by sharing their story and supporting others. They turned their grief into something meaningful—helping children who needed families, speaking up for those who didn’t have a voice, and building a community of care in honor of their daughter. So, if you’re wondering what it means to live with an open heart, maybe it’s this: showing up for others, letting yourself feel deeply, and believing that love—no matter how risky—is always worth it.
